verdicts.detail: correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:battery_aft (the 98 g battery moved to the aft end of the equipment bay -- one plausible cable-routing decision, nothing else changed. It is the exact move the fluids lens list warns about ('the battery that gets relocated for cable routing')): trim -1.74 deg (-14.6 mm bow-to-stern) vs 1.50 limit; freeboard 26.0 mm after trim vs 25 mm required (level flotation would have reported 32.1 mm, so trim costs 6.1 mm); LCG 189.6 vs LCB 212.3 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:top_heavy (mass added on deck, SOLVED for the value that misses this gate's own stated acceptance by 1.15x rather than typed -- a control calibrated to a literal stops being a control the moment the threshold moves. A mast or a light bar is the most common thing added to a finished boat and it always goes up, which is the lens-4 failure exactly): GM 11.1 mm solid, minus 2.4 mm of free surface = 8.7 mm vs 10 mm; the girder divides the bilge into 53 mm cells -- undivided the correction would be 9.4 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:one_big_bay (bulkheads pushed out to 25 mm and 455 mm, which is the obvious move if you want the biggest possible equipment bay and have not thought about flooding. Nothing else changes; the hull, the mass and the loading are identical): sealed compartments support 188 g against an all-up 1143 g -> -954 g margin with the equipment bay full. Foam-filled, so the reserve fails gracefully rather than closed-loop

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:top_heavy_empty (same solved topside mass as boat.free_surface's control, which raises KG in the condition where KG is already highest because the battery -- the heaviest low item -- has been taken out): empty GM 8.7 mm (KG 79.3 mm vs 76.2 loaded) at 42.1 mm draft, vs 10 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:steep_shaft (shaft angle raised to 22 degrees, which is what you reach for when the motor will not clear the hull floor. It is past what a flexible coupler will take and it drags the propeller down into the rudder): shaft angle 22.0 > 12 deg

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:bugged_offset (the inner offset scaled to half, simulating exactly the class of generator bug this project actually hit. The meshes stay watertight and stay valid volumes, which is the point: every other geometry gate passes a mesh with the wrong wall): worst disagreement 50.8% on hull_mid (0.788 mm from mesh volume/area vs 1.60 mm specified); all shells: hull_aft 0.849, hull_bow 0.801, hull_mid 0.788

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:oversize_hull (hull_scale 3.0, i.e. a 900 mm boat. Also the units-slip control: a model that has silently gone metres-for-millimetres somewhere fails here loudly instead of exporting a plausible STL nobody measures): assembled 900 x 349 x 159 mm vs 560 x 230 x 170 mm envelope (worst axis 161%)
